newsitem.title: UK: BASKETBALL-EUROPEANS BATTLE FOR FINAL FOUR SHOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-EUROPEANS BATTLE FOR FINAL FOUR SHOWDOWN.

text.p: After the long slog of winter, club basketball in Europe gets serious on Thursday.
It's down to the last eight with some titanic action in store to decide who contends next month's Final Four championship.
Olympiakos v Panathinaikos tops the bill with all Greece agog at what might happen.
The other clashes pitch Team System Bologna against Barcelona and Turkey's Efes Pilsen against Villeurbanne of France while Stefanel Milan of Italy take on Ljubljana of Slovenia.
The second legs are next Tuesday with any necessary deciders two days after that.
In basketball-crazed Greece 57,000 people are potentially set to see champions Panathinaikos in three possible games against old rivals Olympiakos.
The form-book says Panathinaikos who came through EuroLeague qualifying with the best record of the lot (13-3) from 16 games, while Olympiakos (9-7) suffered several surprising reverses.
There was another setback for Olympiakos when they lost in the first knock-out round at home to Partizan Belgrade two weeks ago and had to return to the Yugoslav capital to clinch the tie 2-1.
By contrast, Panathinaikos booked their quarter-final place 2-0 after a highly impressive 70-55 win in France over former champions Limoges.
As ever, security is a major concern and 7,000 police officers will be on duty for games which many Greeks see as the true European championship.

Spanish fans beg to differ and trust that Barcelona (8-8), after disappointing on several occasions in the EuroLeague, have finally recovered the form which took them to last year's final against Panathinaikos which the Greeks won amid much drama and controversy.
Barcelona's opponents on Thursday, Team System Bologna (12-4) are seeking their best international result.
"It's the mother of all matches. Getting through this round would be a historic result," said the Italian team's spokesman Fabrizio Pungetti.
"Its a very tricky match, we're playing against a great team but we're sure we can do well," said coach Valerio Bianchini.
Serbian playmaker Alexander Djordjevic, one of the Barcelona danger-men, is more familiar to the Bolognese than most opponents since he used to play for Team System.
Stefanel Milan (11-5) should not underestimate Ljubljana (10-6) who edged into the last eight with a battling one-point victory over Cibona Zagreb.
Stefanel go into their match with three straight defeats behind them -- one in the Italian Cup semifinal to Cantu and two, one of them at home, in the domestic championship.
"The most difficult period for the team is ending, we have fewer fixtures and we're getting our energy back," said coach Franco Marcelletti.
"We will have to be committed against a team that maybe lacks great individual talents but that plays a very efficient and physical basketball."
Efes Pilsen (12-4) performed well at the qualifying stage and may just outlast Villeurbanne (12-4) in the other tie.
The Turkish club will again look to their Macedonian star and key playmaker, Petar Naumovski.
Ice-cold under pressure, Naumovski has been the driving force behind Efes' EuroLeague assault, topping the score sheet in nearly every match.
Although weak in their back-court defence, Efes hope that the home advantage and a fully-fit team will see them through to the Final Four, in Rome on April 22-24.
